# Language sketches

Wikipedia-style pages for six living languages of run a24559 (621 living lects), written by `tools/language/sketch.py` from `runs/a24559/languages.json` alone. Regenerate with:

    uv run python tools/language/sketch.py runs/a24559/languages.json --out docs/review/language/sketches --auto

The languages are chosen by criteria, never by id, so a new run picks its own. Each pick must differ from the earlier picks in people and in true family, and (except the conservative pick) in people group: all dragon kinds count as one group, and elves, drow and sea elves as one.

## The English-likeness score

Each component is between 0 and 1; the score is their weighted sum (weights add to 1).

| component | weight | how it is measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| consonants | 0.2 | 1 / (1 + d), d = the mean of (each English consonant's distance to the nearest consonant of the language) and (each of the language's consonants' distance to the nearest English one), in the engine's percept space (place, manner, voicing, airstream, ...) |
| vowels | 0.15 | the same over vowels (height, backness, rounding, length, nasality) |
| syllables | 0.1 | 0.6 x closeness of the largest onset and coda to English's 3 and 4 (1 minus the two gaps added and divided by 7) + 0.4 x the share of closed syllables (full marks at 60%) |
| no tone | 0.1 | 1 if there are no phonemic tones |
| stress | 0.05 | first-syllable stress 1 (the Germanic root-initial pattern), next-to-last 0.75, last 0.5, none 0 |
| word length | 0.05 | 1 minus half the gap between the core-word syllable mean and 1.2 (English core words are mostly one syllable) |
| SVO | 0.07 | SVO 1, free order 0.25 |
| prepositions | 0.05 | prepositions 1, mixed 0.5 |
| articles | 0.06 | 2/3 for a definite article (before the noun 1, after 0.5) + 1/3 for an indefinite article |
| little case | 0.04 | no case 1, a few cases 0.75 (English keeps case in pronouns), many 0 |
| analytic | 0.05 | share of live grammatical markers that are free words or clitics rather than affixes |
| other typology | 0.08 | share of 20 features with English's value as WALS codes it: adjective AN; demonstrative DemN; numeral NumN; relative NRel; alignment nom-acc/neutral; gender sex/none; number sg-pl; pro drop no; wh in situ no; numeral base decimal; passive periphrastic; predicative possession have; copula yes; evidentiality none; numeral classifiers no; negation preverbal; head direction initial; genitive GN/mixed; verb agreement suffix; clusivity no |

English reference inventory (General American: consonants after Ladefoged & Johnson, *A Course in Phonetics* (2015) ch. 2; vowels after Wells, *Accents of English* (1982) and Ladefoged & Johnson table 2.3, monophthongal qualities only (the engine stores no diphthong or rhotic-vowel phonemes, so aɪ aʊ ɔɪ ɚ are left out and FACE, GOAT enter as e, o)):

- consonants (24): p b t d k ɡ tʃ dʒ f v θ ð s z ʃ ʒ h m n ŋ l ɹ j w
- vowels (12): i ɪ e ɛ æ ɑ ɔ o ʊ u ʌ ə

No language in the run can reach English's CCCVCCCC syllable: the engine's largest onset and coda are two consonants each.

## What the output does not record

Things a Wikipedia article would have that these pages cannot show, because the languages file does not hold them: allophones and phonetic detail (sounds are phonemes only); diphthongs as units; intonation; morphophonology beyond the four exemplar nouns and verbs; any sentence-level data (the phrases are assembled from word order and markers); separate inclusive and exclusive 'we' forms, even where the typology says the language has the distinction; case forms of pronouns; root families in the etymology (the word family is inferred from compound and derivation steps); speaker numbers beyond the deme's population estimate; dialect-level variation inside a lect.

The typology features and the live grammatical markers disagree in 320 of the 621 living lects (for example 'no case' with a live locative marker, or 'no number' with a live plural); the pages show both as recorded and flag the clash under Grammar.
